rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Tables 4a-c, 5a-b; the paper reports on-station and on-farm farmer-participatory trial results (yield, water use, net income) and baseline/endline socioeconomic surveys from the ADB-funded project at ten sites in four IGP countries.
rows.notes: The study contains no drip or subsurface drip irrigation treatment and no automated/sensor-triggered irrigation; the irrigation-related technologies it evaluates are laser land leveling, AWD, zero/reduced-till direct seeding, bed planting and canal lining, all under conventional flood irrigation. It reports rice-wheat yields for zero-till systems (Tables 4c, 5b) but not for a ZT-SSD (drip) configuration; in fact double zero-till rice-wheat reduced system productivity by 0.5-0.8 t/ha on-station. The claim about no-till plus automated drip yielding the highest rice-wheat production is not supported by this paper. Q1 is borderline: the paper is a project overview/synthesis that partly reviews component studies (Jat et al 2009, Gathala et al 2009, Mandal et al 2009) but also presents the project's own on-farm trial data and survey results.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Tables 4a-c, 5a-b; the paper reports its own on-station and on-farm trial measurements (water use in mm, yields, costs) and socioeconomic surveys across ten IGP sites.
rows.notes: No tensiometer, soil matric potential threshold, or sensor-based automated irrigation appears anywhere in the study. Water savings reported (e.g., laser leveling -100 to -235 mm, AWD -233 to -490 mm, ZT-DSR 35-40% less irrigation water, canal lining 30-40% saving) come from land leveling, tillage/crop establishment, AWD scheduling and canal lining, not from soil-sensor-triggered irrigation. The 'doubled irrigation water productivity' claim is not a result of this paper.

rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology and Tables 4a-c, 5a-b; the paper reports its own on-station and on-farm yield, water-use and income data and survey results from the project sites.
rows.notes: The study reports yield effects of laser leveling, zero/reduced tillage, drum seeding, LCC-based N management and ICRM packages, but contains no soil-sensor or tensiometer-automated irrigation treatment and therefore no yield result attributable to that technology. The claim of enhanced crop yields from sensor-based automated irrigation is not supported by this paper.

notes: The document is a draft project synthesis (author list and references marked tentative, 'unpublished' data referenced, figures partly garbled). It presents project trial and survey data from the ADB RETA 6208 rice-wheat project but draws heavily on component chapters (Jat et al 2009, Gathala et al 2009, Mandal et al 2009, Singh and Erenstein 2009), so its primary-study status is borderline. None of the three claims (drip irrigation, soil-sensor automated irrigation, ZT-SSD) concern a technology evaluated in this paper; it appears to have been miscited, perhaps confused with later Ladha-group work on subsurface drip in conservation agriculture rice-wheat systems.
